7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V14 keeps the KJV's If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves.

verses.text: Now when Solomon had made an end of praying, the fire came down from heaven, and consumed (burned up) the burnt offering and the sacrifices. And the glory of the LORD filled the house (temple).
And the priests could not enter into the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD's house.

And when all the children of Israel saw how the fire came down, and the glory of the LORD upon the house, they bowed themselves with their faces to the ground upon the pavement (stone floor), and worshipped, and praised the LORD, saying: For He is good, for His mercy endures for ever.
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen, and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated (gave to God) the house of God.

And the priests waited on their offices (stood at their jobs). The Levites also stood with instruments of music of the LORD, which David the king had made to praise the LORD, because His mercy endures for ever, when David praised by their ministry (service). And the priests sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

Moreover (also) Solomon hallowed (made holy) the middle of the court (courtyard) that was before the house of the LORD. For there he offered burnt offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the brasen (bronze) altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt offerings, and the meat offerings (grain offerings), and the fat.
Also at the same time Solomon kept the feast 7 days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation (crowd), from the entering in of Hamath to the river of Egypt.
And in the 8th day they made a solemn assembly (holy meeting). For they kept the dedication of the altar 7 days, and the feast 7 days.

And on the 23rd day of the 7th month Solomon sent the people away into their tents, glad and merry (happy) in heart for the goodness that the LORD had showed to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel His people.

Thus Solomon finished the house of the LORD, and the king's house. And all that came into Solomon's heart to make in the house of the LORD, and in his own house, he prosperously effected (did it with success).
And the LORD appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him: I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place to Myself for an house of sacrifice.
If I shut up heaven so that there be no rain, or if I command the locusts (grasshoppers) to devour (eat up) the land, or if I send pestilence (deadly sickness) among My people,

If My people, which are called by My name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
Now My eyes shall be open, and My ears attent (listening) to the prayer that is made in this place.
For now have I chosen and sanctified (made holy) this house, so that My name may be there for ever. And My eyes and My heart shall be there perpetually (always).
And as for you, if you will walk before Me, as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and shall observe (keep) My statutes (laws) and My judgments (rules),
Then will I stablish (make firm) the throne of your kingdom, according as I have covenanted (made an agreement) with David your father, saying: There shall not fail you a man to be ruler in Israel.
But if you turn away, and forsake (leave) My statutes (laws) and My commandments, which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship them,

Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of My land which I have given them. And this house, which I have sanctified (made holy) for My name, will I cast (throw) out of My sight, and will make it to be a proverb and a byword (something people mock) among all nations.
And this house, which is high, shall be an astonishment (shock) to every one that passes by it, so that he shall say: Why has the LORD done thus to this land, and to this house?

And it shall be answered: Because they forsook (left) the LORD God of their fathers, which brought them forth (out) out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them. Therefore has He brought all this evil upon them.

20.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V15 keeps the KJV's the battle is not yours, but God's. V20 keeps Believe in the LORD your God, so shall ye be established.

verses.text: It came to pass after this also, that the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them other beside the Ammonites, came against Jehoshaphat to battle.
Then there came some that told Jehoshaphat, saying: There comes a great multitude (crowd) against you from beyond the sea on this side Syria. And look, they are in Hazazontamar, which is Engedi.
And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek (look to) the LORD, and proclaimed a fast (announced a time of no eating) throughout all Judah.
And Judah gathered themselves together, to ask help of the LORD. Even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek (look to) the LORD.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation (crowd) of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court (courtyard),

And said: O LORD God of our fathers, are not You God in heaven? And rule not You over all the kingdoms of the heathen (nations)? And in Your hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand (stand against) You?
Are not You our God, who did drive out the inhabitants (people) of this land before Your people Israel, and gave it to the seed (children) of Abraham Your friend for ever?
And they dwelt (lived) in it, and have built You a sanctuary (holy house) in it for Your name, saying:

If, when evil comes upon us, as the sword, judgment, or pestilence (deadly sickness), or famine (no food), we stand before this house, and in Your presence (for Your name is in this house), and cry to You in our affliction (trouble), then You will hear and help.
And now, look, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom You would not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not,
Look, I say, how they reward us, to come to cast (throw) us out of Your possession, which You have given us to inherit (own).
O our God, will You not judge them? For we have no might against this great company (army) that comes against us. Neither know we what to do. But our eyes are upon You.
And all Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.

Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of the LORD in the middle of the congregation (crowd).

And Jahaziel said: Hearken (listen), all Judah, and you inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem, and you king Jehoshaphat. This is what the LORD says to you: Be not afraid nor dismayed (discouraged) by reason of (because of) this great multitude (army). For the battle is not yours, but God's.
To morrow (tomorrow) go down against them. Look, they come up by the cliff of Ziz. And you shall find them at the end of the brook (valley), before the wilderness (desert) of Jeruel.

You shall not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation (saving power) of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Fear not, nor be dismayed (discouraged). To morrow (tomorrow) go out against them, for the LORD will be with you.
And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground. And all Judah and the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, worshipping the LORD.
And the Levites, of the children of the Kohathites, and of the children of the Korhites, stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

And they rose early in the morning, and went forth (out) into the wilderness (desert) of Tekoa. And as they went forth (out), Jehoshaphat stood and said: Hear me, O Judah, and you inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, so shall you be established (made firm). Believe His prophets, so shall you prosper (succeed).

And when Jehoshaphat had consulted with the people, he appointed singers to the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say: Praise the LORD, for His mercy endures for ever.

And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set ambushments (surprise attacks) against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah. And they were smitten (struck down).

For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants (people) of mount Seir, utterly to slay (kill) and destroy them. And when they had made an end of the inhabitants (people) of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness (desert), they looked to the multitude (army), and look, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil (riches) of them, they found among them in abundance (a great amount) both riches with the dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away. And they were 3 days in gathering of the spoil (riches), it was so much.

And on the 4th day they assembled (gathered) themselves in the valley of Berachah (blessing). For there they blessed the LORD. Therefore the name of the same place was called: The valley of Berachah (blessing), to this day.
Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy. For the LORD had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries (stringed instruments) and harps and trumpets to the house of the LORD.
And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of those countries, when they had heard that the LORD fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm (kingdom) of Jehoshaphat was quiet. For his God gave him rest round about.
And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was 35 years old when he began to reign, and he reigned 25 years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
And Jehoshaphat walked in the way of Asa his father, and departed not from it, doing that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
However, the high places (idol altars) were not taken away. For as yet the people had not prepared their hearts to the God of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, look, they are written in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, who is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.
And after this did Jehoshaphat king of Judah join himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who did very wickedly.
And Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah to make ships to go to Tarshish. And they made the ships in Eziongeber.

Then Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying: Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works. And the ships were broken, so that they were not able to go to Tarshish.

verses.text: Josiah was 8 years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem 31 years.
And Josiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the ways of David his father, and declined (turned aside) neither to the right hand, nor to the left.

For in the 8th year of his reign, while he was yet young, Josiah began to seek after the God of David his father. And in the 12th year he began to purge (clean) Judah and Jerusalem from the high places (idol altars), and the groves (Asherah idols), and the carved images, and the molten images (metal idols).

And they brake down (broke down) the altars of Baalim (the Baal idols) in his presence. And the images, that were on high above them, he cut down. And the groves (Asherah idols), and the carved images, and the molten images (metal idols), he brake in pieces (broke in pieces), and made dust of them, and strewed (scattered) it upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
And Josiah burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
And so did he in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon, even to Naphtali, with their mattocks (picks) round about.

And when Josiah had broken down the altars and the groves (Asherah idols), and had beaten the graven images (carved idols) into powder, and cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.

Now in the 18th year of his reign, when he had purged (cleaned) the land, and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder (official record keeper), to repair the house of the LORD his God.

And when they came to Hilkiah the high priest, they delivered (gave) the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant (rest) of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin. And they returned to Jerusalem.

And they put it in the hand of the workmen that had the oversight (were in charge) of the house of the LORD. And they gave it to the workmen that wrought (worked) in the house of the LORD, to repair and amend (fix) the house.
Even to the artificers (craftsmen) and builders gave they it, to buy hewn stone (cut stone), and timber for couplings (joining beams), and to floor the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

And the men did the work faithfully. And the overseers (bosses) of them were Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari. And Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, set it forward (led the work). And other of the Levites, all that could skill of (play) instruments of music.

Also they were over the bearers of burdens (carriers of loads), and were overseers (bosses) of all that wrought (worked) the work in any manner of service. And of the Levites there were scribes (writers), and officers, and porters (doorkeepers).
And when they brought out the money that was brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the LORD given by Moses.
And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe (writer): I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD. And Hilkiah delivered (gave) the book to Shaphan.
And Shaphan carried the book to the king, and brought the king word back again, saying: All that was committed to your servants, they do it.
And they have gathered together the money that was found in the house of the LORD, and have delivered (given) it into the hand of the overseers (bosses), and to the hand of the workmen.
Then Shaphan the scribe (writer) told the king, saying: Hilkiah the priest has given me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.
And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the law, that he rent (tore) his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe (writer), and Asaiah a servant of the king's, saying:

Go, enquire (ask) of the LORD for me, and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that is found. For great is the wrath (anger) of the LORD that is poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD, to do after all that is written in this book.

And Hilkiah, and those the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe (the king's clothes). Now she dwelt (lived) in Jerusalem in the college (second part of the city). And they spoke to her to that effect.
And Huldah answered them: This is what the LORD God of Israel says: Tell the man that sent you to me:

This is what the LORD says: Look, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants (people) of it, even all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah.

Because they have forsaken (left) Me, and have burned incense (sweet-smelling spice) to other gods, so that they might provoke (anger) Me to anger with all the works of their hands, therefore My wrath (anger) shall be poured out upon this place, and shall not be quenched (put out).
And as for the king of Judah, who sent you to enquire (ask) of the LORD, so shall you say to him: This is what the LORD God of Israel says concerning the words which you have heard:

Because your heart was tender, and you did humble yourself before God, when you heard His words against this place, and against the inhabitants (people) of it, and humbled yourself before Me, and did rend (tear) your clothes, and weep before Me, I have even heard you also, says the LORD.

Look, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in peace. Neither shall your eyes see all the evil that I will bring upon this place, and upon the inhabitants (people) of the same. So they brought the king word again.
Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up into the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah, and the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem, and the priests, and the Levites, and all the people, great and small. And he read in their ears all the words of the book of the agreement that was found in the house of the LORD.

And the king stood in his place, and made an agreement before the LORD, to walk after the LORD, and to keep His commandments, and His testimonies, and His statutes (laws), with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the agreement which are written in this book.
And Josiah caused all that were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand to it. And the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem did according to the agreement of God, the God of their fathers.

And Josiah took away all the abominations (hated things) out of all the countries that pertained (belonged) to the children of Israel, and made all that were present in Israel to serve, even to serve the LORD their God. And all his days they departed not from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
